questions.q: What theoretical framework are Shapley values borrowed from?
options: Cooperative game theory
Markov decision processes
Bayesian inference
Convex optimization duality
questions.explain: Shapley values originate in cooperative game theory, which asks how to fairly split a payoff among players who contribute differently depending on who else is already in the game.

questions.q: What guarantees that SHAP's allocation of credit to features is 'fair'?
options: It only considers the single most important feature
It averages each feature's marginal contribution over every possible ordering of features
It assigns equal credit to every feature regardless of its actual effect
It is computed only on the training set
questions.explain: Averaging a feature's marginal contribution across every possible ordering in which features could be added removes bias from which feature happens to be considered first, which is what makes the allocation fair.

questions.q: Which shap explainer is designed for fast, exact computation on tree-based models like random forests or XGBoost?
options: shap.Explainer only
shap.LinearExplainer
shap.TreeExplainer
shap.KernelExplainer only
questions.explain: shap.TreeExplainer(model) is built specifically for tree-based models and computes exact Shapley values efficiently, unlike the slower general-purpose Explainer.

questions.q: What do the SHAP values for a single prediction add up to?
options: Always exactly 1.0, like a probability distribution
The model's training accuracy
The difference between that prediction and the model's average (baseline) prediction
Nothing meaningful -- they are not additive
questions.explain: A core property of Shapley values is additivity: for any individual prediction, the SHAP values across all features sum exactly to (prediction - baseline).

questions.q: In a SHAP summary plot, what does it suggest if a top-ranked feature's contributions are scattered in both directions with no relationship to the feature's own value?
options: The feature is definitely the most important one in the model
The plot was generated incorrectly
It may be a sign the model is picking up noise rather than a genuine, directional signal
The model has zero predictive power at all
questions.explain: A clean signal typically pushes predictions consistently in one direction as the feature's value rises or falls. Scattered, incoherent contributions are a red flag that the model may be fitting noise rather than real signal.
